## Goal

The client runtime agents use and the shell's trusted controls: input that is never lost, converges across tabs and devices, and is submitted only by the human through a control the artifact can't forge.

## Owned requirements

Close each with the check below, through the real public interface (README §3).

| ID | Requirement | Route | Concrete check |
|---|---|---|---|
| AU-08 | The client runtime offers `useField`, `useSubmit`, `useSubmitControl`, `useSignal`, `useAction`, `useLive`, `useChoice`, `useViewer`, `useArtifact`, a react-hook-form adapter and a Claude-compatible `window.storage` (INTERFACES §2.3) | M, B | Each hook of INTERFACES §2.3 has unit tests and a browser test; window.storage passes a compatibility suite modeled on Claude's documented API |
| AU-09 | Multi-page artifacts use a `pages/` convention on React Router, with the history mode chosen per delivery target and the current page reported to the shell | B | pages/ artifact navigates in browser history locally, hash in static export, memory in MCP Apps; comments record the page |
| IN-02 | Autosave flushes on blur, visibility change and before submit; a closed tab loses no saved input | B | Close the tab mid-debounce in three browsers; reopen shows the value (pagehide and journal paths) |
| IN-03 | Tabs and devices viewing the same draft converge through the event stream; overlapping edits surface as conflicts | B | Two tabs and two contexts converge on different fields; same-field edit surfaces a conflict with both choices |
| IN-04 | Offline edits are journaled in IndexedDB and replay in order; edits against incompatible versions are mapped or reported | B | Offline edits journal and replay in order; edits against a replaced version map by ID or become orphans |
| IN-13 | The viewer sees distinct states for submitted, delivered to host and pending delivery | B, R | Shell shows Submitted, Delivered, Pending delivery and Undeliverable in the right sequence (browser); Mirza reviews wording |
| SH-02 | Artifacts can request trusted controls (with labels) but cannot render, click or spoof them; hosts choose whether the artifact submit channel is allowed; every submission records its channel and viewer | B, C | Artifact requests a label; it cannot click or spoof the control; host shell-only policy denies artifact submit with the code; channel recorded |
| VR-04 | A newer version shows a banner in open views; switching is the viewer's choice | B | Open view shows the banner within one event after a publish (browser, three engines) |
| VR-05 | Drafts carry over between versions by stable field ID; unmatched inputs are kept as orphans, shown in a read-only "Not carried over" panel and delivered in a labelled `orphaned` section | I, B | Version with removed field: banner counts orphans, panel shows values read-only, results include `orphaned` (browser + integration) |
| VR-10 | Published versions keep working on newer runtimes: the gateway serves every browser-protocol revision it has shipped, within the deprecation rule | I, B | Fixture version built at browser-protocol revision N works against a gateway at N+1 (CI keeps old fixtures) |
| LL-03 | "Always follow this artifact": a per-viewer choice that loads new versions automatically unless unsaved edits or orphans would result | B | Follow on: new version loads automatically; blocked by unsaved edits or orphans with the banner instead |

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

- `@mostra/react` (all of INTERFACES §2.3 except `useAction` and `useLive`, which come in WP-08);
- autosave and flush rules, multi-tab convergence and the IndexedDB journal;
- `window.storage`, the react-hook-form adapter and router integration;
- the dated browser protocol;
- the shell's trusted Submit and Choose with channel policy, delivery states, the version banner, follow, and the "Not carried over" panel.

Design detail for this package:

- Every hook of INTERFACES §2.3 except `useAction` and `useLive`; `window.storage` per D53; RHF adapter; React Router `pages/` integration with history per target.
- Debounced saves with flush on blur, `visibilitychange`, `pagehide` and before submit; IndexedDB journal; BroadcastChannel latency path.
- Browser protocol revision 1, with a fixture-based compatibility test framework for revisions N and N+1.
- Shell: trusted Submit and Choose honoring channel policy, delivery states, version banner, follow, the 'Not carried over' panel; the visual design follows the round-4 direction and gets its final pass in WP-20.

## Out of scope

- Review overlay and review sets (WP-20)
- Actions and live data hooks (WP-08)

## Acceptance evidence

- Playwright in three browsers: closing a tab loses nothing; two tabs converge; an offline edit replays and a conflict surfaces; a submit from a stale view is flagged;
- the artifact can't click or forge the trusted Submit (synthetic click, overlay and postMessage forgery attempts);
- the banner and follow appear with orphans;
- a version built at browser-protocol revision N works against a gateway at N+1 in a fixture.

Also: `pnpm check` green (from WP-01 on), diff reviewed, evidence matrix rows updated, docs and AGENTS.md current, progress report written after acceptance (README §4).

## Risks and notes

- Forgery tests must include synthetic clicks, overlays covering the shell, and postMessage spoofing from the artifact origin.

## Handoff

One-off artifacts work end to end in the browser; long-lived artifacts have state, follow and policy none.
